note: P-256 point arithmetic needs no signature, so the fixture's ACTUAL compiled locking script runs on @bsv/sdk's Spend engine with concrete points. Every expected point is OpenSSL's (crypto.createECDH('prime256v1') with the scalar as private key), NOT compiler output. The k=2 and P+P spends are the two defects fixed here: p256Mul(G,2n) returned 64 zero bytes and p256Add(G,G) returned a wrong point.

spends.note: p256Mul(G, 2) == 2G — the scalar that returned the all-zero point
p256MulGen(2) == 2G — same ladder, generator entry point
p256Add(G, G) == 2G — the affine doubling case that returned a wrong point
p256Mul(G, 3) == 3G != the committed 2G — proves the accepts are not vacuous

p256Mul(G, n+2) == 2G. Before the scalar reduce landed (f16790a9) the ladder ran over k+3n with the top bit fallen off the end of the loop and returned a DIFFERENT multiple of G. Nothing outside the TS tier had ever executed a k >= n scalar; this is that path on the real Spend engine, in every tier.
p256MulGen(n+2) == 2G — same reduce, generator entry point.

p256Add(G, -G) is the point at infinity, which affine x||y cannot encode, so the emitter returns the ALL-ZERO blob — and p256OnCurve rejects it, which is the first assert in verifyAdd. Selecting the tangent on (px == qx) alone made this return 2G instead: on-curve, plausible, wrong, and ACCEPTED by the same assert. This spend is the cross-tier standing proof that it does not.

GAP-301 on a real engine: the two arguments are ONE group element in two encodings (x = 5 and x + p; this curve has an on-curve point with x small enough that x + p still fits the coordinate width). p256Add compares the RAW x coordinates to detect doubling, so it takes the chord path, divides by (qx - px) = p = 0, and — cFieldInv being Fermat, inv(0) = 0 — returns a point that is neither 2P nor on the curve, from a script that SUCCEEDS. The only thing that can reject it is p256OnCurve, which is verifyAdd's first assert, and which is also where the x < p canonicity guard lives. Nothing outside the TS tier had ever executed a non-canonical coordinate.

N-252: p256Add((5, 0), (5, 0)), an off-curve operand with y = 0 doubled. The tangent (3x^2 - 3)/(2y) has no denominator; cFieldInv is Fermat, inv(0) = 0, so before N-252 the adder returned (p - 10, 0) from a SUCCEEDING add, and only verifyAdd's p256OnCurve assert stopped it. Now the adder itself ABORTS (OP_VERIFY on NOT(cond AND px != 0 AND py == 0)). This spend is rejected before AND after the fix, so it is a standing re-execution of the new bytes, NOT the discriminating proof: that is packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/n252-p256-p384-add-y0.test.ts, which compares the bare p256Add result on Spend.
